definition: Training with a selected subset of negative alternatives instead of all possibilities.
example: Sample nonmatching items for an embedding model.
caveat: The negative distribution influences what is learned.

definition: An outer evaluation loop surrounding an inner model-selection loop.
example: Estimate tuned-model performance without reusing selection folds.
caveat: The extra fits can be expensive.

definition: A momentum variant incorporating a look-ahead correction to the update direction.
example: Accelerate suitable gradient-based training.
caveat: Different implementations can express the update differently.

definition: A parameterized computation built from interconnected layers or units whose outputs are learned from data.
example: Map image pixels to category scores.
caveat: Biological inspiration does not imply a faithful model of the brain.

definition: A model whose hidden-state evolution is defined by an ordinary differential equation with neural-network dynamics.
example: Model continuous-time latent dynamics.
caveat: Solver tolerances and numerical stability affect results.

definition: A computational unit producing an activation from inputs and parameters.
example: Apply an activation to a weighted input sum.
caveat: Modern layers may not map cleanly onto individual neuron metaphors.

definition: Updating parameters using gradient and curvature information to solve an optimization problem.
example: Optimize a small twice-differentiable objective.
caveat: Full Hessian inversion is impractical for large neural models.

definition: A four-bit quantization data type designed around quantiles of a normal distribution.
example: Store base-model weights in QLoRA-style training.
caveat: Its advantage depends on weight distribution and implementation.

definition: Under specified averaging assumptions, no learner outperforms all alternatives on every possible problem.
example: Choose algorithms based on task assumptions.
caveat: It does not say all methods perform equally on real data.

definition: A vector representation of a graph node learned from its attributes or relationships.
example: Represent users in an interaction graph.
caveat: Similar embeddings do not necessarily imply identical graph roles.

definition: A specification of how noise strength changes across diffusion training or sampling time.
example: Control signal-to-noise levels during image generation.
caveat: The best schedule depends on parameterization and sampling procedure.

definition: Learning an unnormalized model by distinguishing data from samples of a known noise distribution.
example: Estimate a language model without full normalization.
caveat: NCE and InfoNCE are related but distinct objectives.

definition: A procedure that removes redundant overlapping detections, typically keeping higher-scoring candidates.
example: Suppress multiple boxes for the same object.
caveat: Aggressive suppression can remove genuinely overlapping objects.

definition: Optimization where the objective or feasible set lacks convexity.
example: Train a deep neural network.
caveat: Nonconvexity does not imply every practical solution is poor.

definition: Factoring a nonnegative matrix into lower-dimensional nonnegative factors.
example: Find additive parts or document themes.
caveat: Solutions are generally nonunique.

definition: Change over time in a process's distributional characteristics.
example: Handle shifting demand patterns.
caveat: Nonstationarity does not identify the cause of the change.

definition: A function measuring the size of a vector or matrix under specified rules.
example: Measure a gradient's magnitude before clipping.
caveat: Different norms induce different geometries.

definition: A continuous bell-shaped distribution determined by mean and variance.
example: Model additive measurement noise.
caveat: Real-world tails may be heavier than Gaussian.

definition: Rescaling values under a specified convention, such as unit vector length or a fixed range.
example: Scale each document vector to unit length.
caveat: The word is overloaded; specify the operation.

definition: A generative model that transforms a simple distribution through invertible mappings with tractable density change.
example: Model a complex distribution while evaluating its likelihood.
caveat: Invertibility and Jacobian tractability constrain the architecture.

definition: Detecting new observations unlike a reference dataset assumed mostly normal.
example: Flag unfamiliar behavior after training on normal activity.
caveat: Training-set outlier detection is a related but different setup.

definition: A specified statistical claim used as the reference for a hypothesis test.
example: Assume two systems have equal mean performance.
caveat: Failing to reject it does not prove it true.

definition: A calculation producing a magnitude too large for its numeric representation.
example: Diagnose infinite losses during unstable training.
caveat: An infinite result can contaminate later computations.

definition: The extent to which a computation avoids excessive error amplification or invalid numeric values.
example: Compute softmax without overflowing exponentials.
caveat: Mathematically equivalent formulas can have different floating-point behavior.

definition: A nonzero value becoming too small to represent normally, potentially rounding toward zero.
example: Detect gradients lost in low-precision training.
caveat: Subnormal handling depends on the format and hardware.

definition: Approximating a kernel matrix using a subset of its columns or landmark points.
example: Reduce kernel-method memory requirements.
caveat: Landmark selection affects approximation quality.

definition: Predicting object categories and their locations, commonly as bounding boxes.
example: Locate every vehicle in a street image.
caveat: Detection differs from labeling every pixel.

definition: A scalar criterion optimized during learning, potentially combining data loss, penalties, and constraints.
example: Minimize prediction loss plus regularization.
caveat: An optimized objective is only a proxy for the real goal.

definition: The ability to understand system behavior using signals such as logs, metrics, and traces.
example: Investigate a failed multi-step model workflow.
caveat: Logging everything is neither necessary nor automatically privacy-preserving.

definition: Information available to an agent from the environment at a particular step.
example: An image from a robot camera.
caveat: Observation and underlying state need not be identical.

definition: The ratio of odds between two conditions or groups.
example: Interpret a logistic-regression coefficient after exponentiation.
caveat: An odds ratio is not a risk ratio or a probability difference.

definition: Distillation using examples or trajectories not sampled from the current student policy.
example: Train on a fixed teacher-generated dataset.
caveat: The training distribution may differ from student behavior at deployment.

definition: Estimating a target policy's performance using data collected by another policy.
example: Evaluate a new ranking policy from logged interactions.
caveat: Poor action overlap can make estimates unreliable.

definition: Learning about a policy using data generated by a different behavior policy.
example: Train from a replay buffer or logged actions.
caveat: Distribution mismatch must be handled appropriately.

definition: Distillation using a fixed teacher or precomputed teacher outputs.
example: Train from a saved teacher-probability dataset.
caveat: Offline and off-policy describe different aspects.

definition: Learning a policy from a fixed dataset without collecting new environment interactions during training.
example: Use historical interaction logs.
caveat: Unsupported actions can lead to severe extrapolation errors.

definition: Executing model predictions locally on the user's or application's device.
example: Run a small language model without a network request.
caveat: Local execution still has memory, energy, and security constraints.

definition: Distillation using trajectories or outputs sampled from the current student policy for teacher feedback.
example: Query teacher probabilities on student-generated prefixes.
caveat: Teacher access and sampling cost can be substantial.

definition: Learning principally from data produced by the policy being updated or evaluated.
example: Update a policy from fresh trajectories.
caveat: Practical implementations may tolerate limited policy lag.

definition: A support-vector method estimating a region containing typical training examples.
example: Detect departures from a known normal class.
caveat: Kernel scale and contamination assumptions are influential.

definition: Representing categories with indicator coordinates.
example: Encode red, green, and blue as separate binary columns.
caveat: High-cardinality features can create very wide matrices.

definition: Learning or adapting from one example per new task or category.
example: Recognize a new symbol after one demonstration.
caveat: A one-shot prompt is not necessarily weight training.

definition: Distillation where teacher signals or teacher/student models are updated during the training process.
example: Train peers jointly with mutual prediction targets.
caveat: Online does not necessarily mean on-policy.

definition: Producing predictions in response to arriving requests within an operational latency budget.
example: Answer an interactive application request.
caveat: Online inference does not imply online model training.

definition: Updating a model incrementally as new observations arrive.
example: Update a predictor after each data batch.
caveat: Online does not mean merely connected to the internet.

definition: Identifying inputs likely outside the model's intended data distribution.
example: Route unfamiliar inputs to human review.
caveat: High confidence does not rule out OOD inputs.

definition: Converting text appearing in images or scanned documents into machine-readable text.
example: Extract receipt text for later processing.
caveat: OCR errors can propagate into downstream language-model answers.

definition: Searching for parameters or decisions that improve a specified objective.
example: Reduce model loss using gradient updates.
caveat: Optimization success is not the same as task success.

definition: An algorithm that updates trainable parameters using gradients or other information.
example: Use AdamW for neural-network training.
caveat: The optimizer does not define the full training procedure.

definition: Persistent values used by an optimizer, such as momentum and second-moment estimates.
example: Store Adam's moving averages.
caveat: Optimizer state can consume more memory than model weights.
